sample_design: Eight previously unaudited identities across five manufacturers, selected before classification to stress a materially different post-PR60 region: wearable/wrist anchors, rigid bucket-lip anchors, tool-side retrofit attachments, and one conventional tether control. The cohort intentionally excludes all V1-V3 identities and the three products used for the PR61 vertical proof.
audit_question: After vertically proving PR #60's belt/beam/rail AnchorAttachment installation model through normal first-party ingestion, do materially different wearable and rigid hook-on anchor families plus fresh tool-side controls now land predominantly in A/B without a comparable recurring C/D seam?
decision: Do not shift the development centre to catalogue throughput yet. The fresh cohort is not predominantly A/B, and its four C cases form two independent recurring cross-vendor seams rather than SKU exceptions: worker-worn wrist anchors require a reusable primary-anchor feature/installation representation, while aerial-bucket hooks require a reusable bucket-lip/edge feature plus hook-on or clip-on installation semantics. D remains zero and the four B cases continue to support the existing throughput signal, so the next semantic work should stay narrowly focused on these repeated anchor-installation families rather than widening downstream compatibility, ranking, selection or exhaustion rules.

products.name: Wrist Attachment Anchor; adjustable UniFit size with Speed-clip and D-ring
observed_public_facts: adjustable wristband anchor intended for close-proximity tool tethering
wrist attachment anchor provides both Speed-clip and D-ring connection points
cuff band and strap use neoprene/polyester and nylon components
5 lb maximum tool capacity
core_fit: anchor_attachment_tether_side connection interfaces can represent the provided D-ring/clip sides once extracted
PR #60 installation rules can retain an exact selected feature once a supported PrimaryAnchorFeature kind exists
required_core_changes: extend the reusable PrimaryAnchorFeature vocabulary to represent a worker wrist or equivalent worker-worn anchor feature, with evidence-backed wearable fastening/retention semantics rather than treating the body as a belt/beam/rail
preserve the selected worker-worn feature through the existing AnchorInstallationBinding path without changing tether-to-anchor compatibility
products.portability_gap: PR #60 can prove installation only against belt, beam or rail features. This product's defining primary-anchor target is the worker's wrist, so normal ingestion cannot compile truthful installation eligibility without either a reusable worker-worn feature or an invalid belt/rail analogy. No published wrist size is inferred from UniFit wording.

products.name: Adjustable Wrist Anchor - 2.5kg / 5.5lb
observed_public_facts: adjustable wristband incorporates a built-in load-rated tether anchor
manufacturer describes it as designed to fit all wrist sizes
industrial-grade hook-and-loop closure secures the adjustable band
2.5 kg / 5.5 lb maximum load
evidence_notes: The qualitative all-sizes wording is not a numeric fit envelope and must not be converted into wrist dimensions.
core_fit: generic attachment-interface facts can be ingested without SKU-pair logic
existing AnchorInstallationBinding provenance can carry a resolved installation after the target feature is representable
required_core_changes: the same reusable worker-worn/wrist PrimaryAnchorFeature seam exposed independently by FallTech 5331A1
an evidence-backed adjustable-band fastening rule that can bind to that concrete wrist feature without inventing geometry from one-size wording
products.portability_gap: This independently repeats the FallTech wrist-anchor gap. Belt/beam/rail cannot truthfully stand in for a wrist, and the current wrap/cinch/thread_over vocabulary does not by itself establish the worker-worn target or the adjustable wristband's installation conditions.

products.name: Locking Aerial Bucket Hook with Tethering Point - 2in
observed_public_facts: 2 inch variant quickly attaches to a standard aerial-bucket lip
self-locking exterior hook automatically locks when load is applied
enclosed tethering point is rated for 7 lb / 3.2 kg dynamic tool-lanyard load
hook body is rated for 40 lb / 18.14 kg static hold
core_fit: load-bearing component and tether-side interface facts
numeric dimensions can remain evidence facts once a relevant feature dimension exists
existing AnchorInstallationBinding can preserve exact installation provenance after eligibility is proven
required_core_changes: add a reusable primary-anchor lip/edge feature kind suitable for aerial-bucket lips rather than overloading rail
add an evidence-backed hook-on or clip-on AnchorAttachment installation method that evaluates one concrete lip/edge feature, including explicit dimensional bounds only where published
products.portability_gap: The product clips onto a bucket lip; it does not wrap, cinch or thread over a belt/beam/rail. The current PR #60 vocabulary therefore cannot prove its installation without a new reusable edge/lip target and hook-on installation family.

products.name: 3-Inch Gated Bucket Hook
observed_public_facts: attaches to a standard 3 inch / 7.6 cm lip aerial bucket
lockable latch helps reduce the risk of tools falling
4 foot tether-rated attachment point supports tools up to 7 lb
40 lb / 18.1 kg maximum static load
core_fit: load-bearing component and tether-side interface facts
rated capacity and explicit lip dimension evidence
existing exact binding/provenance path after installation eligibility is representable
required_core_changes: the same reusable bucket-lip/edge PrimaryAnchorFeature seam exposed independently by Ergodyne Squids 3178
the same generic hook-on/clip-on installation family, with the published 3 inch lip requirement kept as an explicit feature bound rather than a product-size guess
products.portability_gap: Klein independently demonstrates that rigid bucket-lip hooks are a real cross-vendor anchor family. Mapping the bucket lip to rail or pretending the hook is a wrap/cinch/thread-over installation would erase the manufacturer's actual installation semantics.

products.name: 5pc 2lb D-Ring Web Attachment
observed_public_facts: D-ring web attachment creates a secure tether point on tools without a lanyard hole
manufacturer requires Milwaukee Self-Adhering Tape for installation
metal D-ring provides the tethering connection point
2 lb maximum tool load
products.portability_gap: This is the already-modeled tape/wrap plus required-pairing architecture in a fresh Milwaukee identity. The missing work is Milwaukee ToolAttachment acquisition/extraction and evidence-bound pairing, not a new downstream primitive.

products.name: Wire Tool Attachment - Screw Gate Tool Tail - 3lbs / 1.4kg
observed_public_facts: wire screw-gate tail threads through a captive tool hole and screws closed to complete the loop
manufacturer states compatibility with captive holes 0.2 in / 5 mm or larger
3 lb / 1.4 kg maximum working capacity
48 in / 122 cm maximum tether length
core_fit: minimum opening geometry as an evidence-backed feature constraint
rated capacity and maximum tether-length constraint
products.portability_gap: The post-PR #53 single-feature captive-through-opening eligibility seam already represents the target feature without widening to handles. Ergodyne ingestion must preserve the screw-gate closure and 5 mm minimum-hole evidence, but no new recommendation primitive is required.

products.name: 5 lb Speed-clip Tool Attachment with choke-on cinch-loop
observed_public_facts: choke-on design is intended for tools with existing captive eye holes
Speed-clip provides an interchangeable tether-side connection
manufacturer states compatibility with Speed-clip compatible 5 lb tool tethers and the wrist anchor
5 lb maximum tool capacity
core_fit: manufacturer-declared connector/interface compatibility without SKU-pair hard-coding
products.portability_gap: FallTech extraction must onboard the Speed-clip vocabulary and declarations, but the existing generic clip/connector attributes plus evidence-bound manufacturer compatibility relation can carry the semantics without a FallTech-specific downstream branch.

products.name: Tool Tether, 10-Pound Maximum Load
observed_public_facts: manufacturer instructs attaching the carabiner end to the anchor point
warnings require the cinch to remain snug while in use
32 inch relaxed and 60 inch stretched lengths
10 lb / 4.5 kg maximum working capacity
products.portability_gap: The current Klein adapter is tool-only. This tether needs Klein catalogue extraction for endpoint topology, explicit direction, cinch evidence, length and capacity, but those facts already fit the neutral tether core.
